'''Charles Gilbert Overberger''' (October 12, 1920 – March 17, 1997) was an [[Americans|American]] chemist, specialising in [[polymer]] research and education.<ref name=obit/>

==Biography==
Overberger was born in [[Barnesboro, Pennsylvania]] on October 12, 1920.

In 1941, he was awarded a B.Sc. at the [[Pennsylvania State University]] where he was a member of [[Sigma Pi]] fraternity, [[Phi Eta Sigma]] honor society, and [[Phi Lambda Upsilon]] honor society.<ref>{{cite book | title=La Vie Yearbook | publisher=Pennsylvania State University | issue=v. 44 | year=1941 | url=https://digital.libraries.psu.edu/digital/collection/lavie/id/16716/rec/53 | access-date=December 7, 2021 | page=115}}</ref> He received his Ph.D. at the [[University of Illinois]] in 1944, where he continued to work as a research assistant for two years.<ref name = "Emerald">{{cite magazine|last=|first=|date=Spring 1966|volume=53|number=1|magazine=The Emerald of Sigma Pi|title=Chemical Society President|page=270|url=http://www.enivation.com/SigmaPi/archive/Emerald/1966/SP_EMERALD_VOL_53_NO_1_SPRING_1966.pdf |url-status=usurped| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160701004919/http://www.enivation.com/SigmaPi/archive/Emerald/1966/SP_EMERALD_VOL_53_NO_1_SPRING_1966.pdf | archive-date = July 1, 2016}}</ref>

From 1946 to 1947, he had a DuPont Post-Doctoral Fellowship at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], then became assistant professor of chemistry at the [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]].
In 1951, he became professor and associate director of the Polymer Research Institute. Between 1955 and 1963, he was chairman of the chemistry department, and from 1964 to 1967 dean of science and director of the Polymer Research Institute.
He was [[president of the American Chemical Society]] in 1967.<ref name = Emerald/>
After that, he joined the [[University of Michigan]] as professor and chair of chemistry, where he also acted as vice president for research from 1972 to 1983.
He founded the Macromolecular Research Center in 1968, and was director until 1987. He retired two years later.

Overberger died in Riverview, [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], of [[Parkinson's disease]] on March 17, 1997.<ref name=obit>{{cite web |url=http://ur.umich.edu/9697/Mar25_97/obit.htm |title=Charles Overberger |access-date=2015-02-25 |quote=Charles G. Overberger, professor emeritus of chemistry and vice president emeritus for research, died March 17 at Riverview of Ann Arbor after an extended illness resulting from Parkinson's Syndrome and related disorders. He was 76. |publisher=[[University of Michigan]] |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304141813/http://www.ur.umich.edu/9697/Mar25_97/obit.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* [[Charles Lathrop Parsons Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]] (1978)
* International Award of the [[Society of Plastics Engineers]] (1979)
* [[Howard N. Potts Medal]] from the [[Franklin Institute]] (1982)<ref name="PottsMedal_Laureates">{{cite web|url=http://www.fi.edu/winners/show_results.faw?gs=&ln=&fn=&keyword=&subject=&award=POTTS&sy=&ey=&max=300&name=Submit |title=Franklin Laureate Database - Howard N. Potts Medal Laureates |publisher=[[Franklin Institute]] |access-date=March 13, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502215246/http://www.fi.edu/winners/show_results.faw?gs=&ln=&fn=&keyword=&subject=&award=POTTS&sy=&ey=&max=300&name=Submit |archive-date=May 2, 2014 }}</ref>
* [[University of Michigan]]'s Distinguished Faculty Achievement Award (1985)
